---
title: "A common report for race and gender gaps"
subtitle: "5.7 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), one report for two criteria"
description: "Weighted expected-risk evaluation of a common report and two fixed KRW cards."
---

A common report assigns the same firm grades for race and gender contact gaps. The race weight determines
how much errors on each gap contribute to the loss. The scatterplot shows the selected grades. The risk chart
evaluates the common report and KRW's two published cards at the same weight and withholding cost.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **“Equal weights.”** At the original cost, the common report's risk .2455 is below the risk of withholding every comparison. Both published cards have higher risk than withholding every comparison.
- **“Race .80.”** The race card crosses the withholding line near race weight .69. **“Gender .80”** shows the opposite crossing near .29.
- **“Color firms by this report.”** The risk uses the current cost and the selected card's original grades. Select a firm in the scatterplot or table, or use the selector, to read both marginal intervals.
- **“Most grades allowed in the live order search.”** For each cap, the app gives the number of reports searched and lists the reports tied for the lowest risk. Grade one ranks highest. A shared grade leaves a comparison unstated.

The browser combines each firm's average posterior ranks with the current weights and searches cuts of the resulting order. At the original equal weights, cost, and cap, it reproduces the archived result from a search over all capped reports. The archived status, bound, and gap apply to that original search. Each published KRW card was chosen under its own objective. Its risk here answers how the fixed card performs under the current loss. See [the original report card](../uncertainty/case-zero.qmd) for its interpretation.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The separate race and gender fits give marginal intervals and expected losses for each gap. Estimating how the gaps vary together in the posterior would require a joint fit. The scatterplot instead shows variation across firms in the historical experiment. These experimental data do not describe firms’ current conduct. Data: Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), doi:10.1257/aer.20230700; deposit doi:10.3886/E198284V1, CC-BY-NC as stated by the deposit (no version), noncommercial use only; as adapted in postrank 1.1.0. Changes: continuous cells with central intervals in place of KRW’s posterior grids, supplied comparison probabilities, archived common report and browser order searches. No endorsement implied. <details class="prx-recipe">
<summary>In postrank</summary>

This call loads the released analysis and evaluates both published cards under its common loss.

```r
library(postrank); source(system.file("scripts", "_vignette-setup.R", package = "postrank"))
krw <- load_or_compute("case_krw_signed97"); cards <- pr_case_krw$reference$single_criterion$grade
postrank_compare(krw, race_card = cards$race, gender_card = cards$gender, baselines = character())$table
```
</details>

Standalone: [embed/krw-two.html](../../embed/krw-two.html), for example `?w=.8&report=race`.
